instruction: Complete the task with a suitable choice from ANSYS, Abaqus, and AutoCAD. For the steps below, launch Abaqus CAE or AutoCAD 2024 from their desktop shortcuts; ANSYS MAPDL is available at `C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\ansys\bin\winx64\ANSYS261.exe`. Use the selected tool to perform a constrained thermal stress analysis (Case B). Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch an 8 mm x 8 mm rectangle in the Y-Z plane (Y from 0 to 8, Z from 0 to 8) and extrude along the global X-axis to a length of 120 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Aluminum with Young's modulus E = 70000 MPa, Poisson's ratio nu = 0.33, and thermal expansion coefficient = 2.3e-5 /K. Create a Solid Homogeneous section using Aluminum and assign it to the entire bar. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the bar. Analysis Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-Thermal-B. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply a predefined temperature field of 20 degC to the whole model in the Initial step. Constrain both end faces with U1 = U2 = U3 = 0: the left end face at X = 0 and the right end face at X = 120 mm. In Step-Thermal-B, apply a predefined temperature field of 100 degC to the whole model. Discretization: Mesh the bar with a global seed size of 6 mm. Assign the element type appropriate three-dimensional solid element formulation and generate the mesh. Job Execution: Create a job named Job-ThermalStress-B, submit it for analysis, and wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and the native solver result artifact into `C:\Users\user\Desktop\result`. Save only the files from the selected tool. Software launch locations: Abaqus/CAE: `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Abaqus CAE.lnk`; ANSYS: multiple ANSYS launch shortcuts are available under `C:\Users\Public\Desktop`; choose the most suitable ANSYS shortcut for the task; AutoCAD 2024: `C:\Users\Public\Desktop\AutoCAD 2024.lnk`.
